target_customer: Individuals and teams needing powerful cloud computers, later developers and data scientists training AI models on cloud GPUs
problem: Powerful hardware for simulations and creative work was expensive and tied to a desk. Later, AI developers needed accessible GPU compute and tools without enterprise cloud complexity.
business_model: Usage-based cloud desktops and GPU compute, with subscriptions for Gradient notebooks
product_category: Cloud desktops, then GPU cloud and ML platform

founders.name: Dillon Erb
education: University of Michigan, M.Arch 2014 (Taubman College); studied philosophy as an undergraduate
founders.background_notes: Later co-founded Autonomous Technologies Group (YC F25) per YC page.

founders.name: Daniel Kobran
education: University of Michigan, M.Arch 2014 (Taubman College); environmental design as an undergraduate
founders.background_notes: Later co-founded Autonomous Technologies Group per YC page.

competitors.name: VMware, Citrix and Amazon WorkSpaces
competitors.what: Enterprise remote desktop and virtual desktop products

competitors.name: VNC and Microsoft RDP
competitors.what: Remote access protocols the company said could not match full HD streaming

technical_complexity.rationale: Streaming low latency full HD desktops from GPU servers using Xen and Nvidia GRID on leased colocation hardware was hard for seven people.

defensibility.rationale: Hyperscalers could offer similar virtual desktops and GPUs; the early edge was being first with GPU standard desktops (company claim) and simplicity.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Hyperscalers added GPU instances and managed desktops over time; Paperspace shifted to AI and was bought by DigitalOcean in July 2023.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2015-03-03) described founders who needed expensive hardware for simulations that took days to run; enterprise virtual desktops were an existing paid category.

branding.name_origin: Named as a nod to early AutoCAD (University of Michigan Taubman College profile, 2021-05-07).

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission stated as radical simplicity and straightforward pricing (YC page).

branding.brand_signature: Gradient community notebooks, launched in 2019, a free GPU notebook service

rebrands.why: Became part of DigitalOcean after acquisition; website banner says Paperspace is now part of DigitalOcean

branding.community_and_virality: More than 400,000 users by 2021 and a free Gradient Community Notebooks offering (Michigan profile 2021; press release 2019).

brand_strength.rationale: A recognizable developer brand with a large free community and named customers, but no sourced press about the brand itself.

pivots.to: Gradient, a platform for training AI models on cloud GPUs
pivots.why: Shift toward GPU cloud and ML tools; Gradient launched March 2018 per SiliconANGLE summary in search results

outcome_analysis: Paperspace began as cloud desktops, raised a $4M seed in 2016 and a $13M Series A in 2018, then pivoted into GPU cloud and the Gradient ML platform as AI demand grew. It built a community of over 400,000 users and sold to DigitalOcean for $111 million in cash in July 2023.
notes: Total raised is reported as $35M before acquisition (Orrick summary) and nearly $30M in 2021 (Michigan), while the 2018 round brought the total to $19M per search summary, so a later round of roughly $11M to $16M probably exists but was not found; coverage is partial. Founding year 2014 versus YC 2015. Seed headline URL says series-a but the article text says seed. Earlier undisclosed 2015 investor Zillionize appears in a search summary only.
